failure_summary: render_decision.requiredSet obliges only opp-key-square (c3r1), opp-key-line (windows:c3r1..c6r1) and better-col (col3) while leaving the fork's own squares — opp-fork-pivot (c6r1), opp-double (windows:c3r1,c7r1) and opp-fork-square (c7r1) — merely offered, so all 3/3 runs narrate a double_threat punishment without naming the square that creates it: opponentPunishment.finalMovestring 44315 puts the opponent disc on c6r1 and only then does visualize_board report 'Major threats: col3 row1 (X) [GT]   col7 row1 (X) [GT]'.
notes: A7c fails 3/3: the mechanism rests on the opponent's double threat, the creating square is c6r1 (the 5th move of opponentPunishment.finalMovestring 44315, board-verified), the handle opp-fork-pivot=c6r1 IS offered in render_decision.zones.aliases, yet no run names column 6 — run 2 names only the finishing square c7r1. A7b fails runs 0 and 1: 'hit the fork almost immediately after' / 'sets up a double threat very quickly' promise a specific board object while only c3r1 and the c3-c6 line are located; c7r1 (opp-fork-square) and opp-double are offered and unused, so the fork resolves to nothing findable. Run 2 passes A7b (names column 7). A5 passes 3/3 including A5b (player===2 AND boardState==='opening'): no run says the player is lost and each carries a hold-the-line frame ('the central move was the tough defense', 'Column 3 is the tougher defensive choice', 'makes it harder for your opponent'); the word 'punishment' is supplied verbatim by the render's own frame ('The punishment lands almost at once') and is plain English, not a field-name echo. A3/A4 pass on runs 0-1: c3r1 empty after the played move (board 4431), the c3-c6 bottom-row window and the c3r1/c7r1 fork are all real on 44315, and the timing claim matches register 'immediate'. Sub-sampled per instructions: A3, A4, G2, G4, G5 were graded on runs 0 and 1 only; run 2 is null on those. A1/A2/A6/G7a/G7b copied verbatim from the mechanical json (all pass). HARNESS NOTE, not charged as an axis: run 1 omits the required handle better-col entirely (raw has no [zone:better-col]); production would have retried on that, but compute.mjs does not exercise the retry (OI-183), so this is a known eval artifact rather than a served defect — prose still names column 3, so A6 passes.
